newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks at new intraday record.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks at new intraday record.

text.p: Mexican shares sharply extended their initial advance in early trade on Thursday to break the 4,600-point barrier for the first time ever.
Dealers said share prices gained on carryover from records set the day before, with the Dow Jones bolstering key ADRs and blue chips in turn.
The blue chip IPC share index was up 48.24 points, or 1.06 percent, to a trading record of 4,607.47.
"Basically it took off because of the Dow (Jones)," a floor trader said. "Most ADRs are up on Wall Street, and that inevitably helps us down here."
Dealers said foreign investors were also driving the bourse by buying ahead of Friday's July 4 Independence Day holiday on U.S. markets.
"Foreigners are definitely stepping in; Wall Street closes early today, so they are snapping up stocks as they will miss a day of probable gains in Mexico," another floor trader said.
"It's amazing, foreigners are flooding in. It looks very solid; it's like crazy down here," a desk trader added.
Trading volume had picked up from a moderate open to a brisk total of 10.1 million shares.

Dealers said financial stocks were strong as a brighter outlook for interest rates, confirmed by Wednesday's Federal Open market Committee decision not to raise U.S. base rates, would ease their heavy past-due loans burdens.
In addition, traders said, construction stocks were in demand due to an expected government plan to restructure debts for highway concessionaires.
Market heavyweight Telefonos de Mexico (Telmex) was hauling the market on the back of its ADRs, dealers said. (( --Martin Roberts, Mexico City newsroom +525 728-7907))
